issue: supnṓd 'from sleep' for 'death': *supnós is 'sleep' in every reflex (Gk húpnos, OCS sъnъ); 'death' is at best a euphemism (*mr̥tís/*mr̥tóm would be literal). ph₂tér voc. keeps suffix accent; vocatives are initial-accented (Ved. pítar, Gk páter).
woséyeti is 3sg, but the English is 'You clothe the branches' in a 2sg address (cf. stéygʰesi just before); should be woséyesi.
stóygʰoysu énu: *énu/*ánu governs the accusative (Ved. ánu + acc.), so it should be stóygʰons énu. h₁áyto (aorist 'received') for the gnomic 'receives' is acceptable as an injunctive.

wewkond lacks the root labiovelar: the reduplicated aorist of *wekʷ- is wéwkʷond (Ved. ávocan); as written it is no form of 'say'. Secondary: 'wept' (if from *webʰ- 'weave', expect wébʰt); the closing quote is missing.

m̥rént: zero grade before a vowel-initial ending is *mr-ént, with consonantal m (Ved. mriyáte), not syllabic m̥. Hn̥dʰí for 'below' is doubtful: its main cognate Ved. ádhi means 'on, over'; the secure 'under' is *n̥dʰér/*n̥dʰós (Ved. adhás, Lat. infrā, Goth. undar).

Old non-laryngeal notation (owis, eḱwōs for h₂ówis, h₁éḱwōs), no accents, and kʷe written as a free word instead of an enclitic (eḱwōs-kʷe). The meaning is right but it clashes with the corpus orthography.

séh₂ linékʷti for 'she leaves (departs)': *leykʷ- is transitive 'leave behind' (Ved. riṇákti, Lat. linquit); léytt/léyteti 'go away' would fit. Otherwise excellent (Vala myth: widés ... gʷṓs h₁régʷesi).
ph₂tér voc. accent should be initial, not on the suffix (Ved. pítar, Gk páter). Otherwise sound; sóh₂wl̥ widóyh₁me matches Ved. paśyema sū́ryam.
deywóh₁ is nom. DUAL (or instr. sg.), not plural 'the gods', and it is the subject of 3pl kʷḱént; should be deywṓs.

sérpontih₂ (fem. participle) on h₁ógʷʰis: the dragon word is masculine in its main reflexes (Ved. áhi-, Av. aži-, Gk óphis/ékhis), so expect sérponts. This follows the lexicon's gender f. ph₂tér voc. accent (Ved. pítar). gʷʰéns h₁ógʷʰim is the right formula.
dyéwi Hn̥dʰí 'beneath the sky': Hn̥dʰí 'under' is doubtful (Ved. ádhi = 'on, over'); *n̥dʰér is the secure 'under'. The rest is fine (urvī́ mahī́ pairing, ḱlutóm h₁nómn̥ dʰeh₁-).

ǵʰémi drops the initial dʰ of *dʰǵʰ-: loc. should be dʰǵʰémi (Ved. kṣámi, Hitt. taknī). h₂éwsterōy (dat. sg.) fails to agree with wédn̥bʰos (abl. pl.); expect h₂éwsteroybʰos. Hn̥dʰí 'under' is doubtful (see 55732414).
h₁eǵ ... bʰréh₂tēr-kʷe kʷḱyéh₁m̥: a conjoined subject 'I and my brother' takes a 1st dual/plural verb (kʷḱih₁wé/kʷḱih₁mé), not 1sg.
ph₂tér voc. accent should be initial (Ved. pítar, Gk páter). Otherwise strong: h₁uséwōm déh₃tor, h₁wérHum lowkóm (Ved. urúṃ lokám), HéHḱuns h₁éḱwons.

The Lehmann–Zgusta text with its editorial apparatus left in running text: 'eḱwobʰ(y)os (eḱwomos)' gives alternatives, not one text. Pre-laryngeal notation (owis, aǵontm̥, nerm̥), no accents. The meaning matches.
ǵʰlíeti is ill-formed (no glide; a yé-present would be ǵʰliyéti), and its 'shine' sense is thin (Gk khlíō 'be warm'). Otherwise a good Agni hymn (wéǵʰtor, knower of paths, messenger).
dyéw toy ph₂tér: voc. accent should be initial (Ved. pítar). Otherwise excellent (deywṓs h₁uséwōm déh₃tores, gʷm̥té ... sdté ... ph₃té).
uh₁itéysu: the i-stem loc. pl. is zero-grade *-i-su (Ved. -iṣu, Lith. -isu), so expect uh₁itísu / wéh₁itisu, not full-grade -éy-su.

deywṓm is gen. pl. but is the subject of ǵeǵn̥h₁ḗr ('The gods are born from you'); should be nom. pl. deywṓs. Minor: h₂m̥bʰí for 'in exchange' (the lexicon allows it; *h₂énti, Gk antí, is the usual 'in return for').
túH ... lowkéyonti: 3pl verb with an explicit 2sg subject; should be lowkéyesi (as in the next two clauses).
h₁iménsu: the loc. pl. of men-stems has a zero-grade suffix *-mn̥-su (Ved. -masu), so expect h₁imn̥sú, not full-grade -mén-su.
uh₁itéysu: the i-stem loc. pl. should be zero-grade *-isu (uh₁itísu), not -éysu. Otherwise very good (léyǵʰsi sélpos, sodéyont, wéǵʰe ... tóns n̥smé).
tā́m (fem.) resumes h₁ógʷʰim; the serpent word is masculine in Vedic, Avestan and Greek, so expect tóm. This follows the lexicon's gender f.
